b: The process configurator for its DMC sanding machines helps operators select processing parameters and configure equipment.
The AI-based process configurator is integrated into SCM’s DMC machines for sanding wood and metal

One of the key challenges facing the manufacturing industry is the shortage of specialised technical skills on the factory floor. To address this, SCM Group has developed an innovation for mechanical surface finishing processes, which received an award on 4 Nov at the 20th edition of SMAU in Milan.

The technology is an AI-based process configurator integrated into its DMC machines for sanding wood and metal. It draws on decades of accumulated data and scientific testing to provide a digital assistant that guides SCM’s sales teams in machine configuration and helps operators select suitable processing parameters.

Operations such as sanding, calibration and deburring require precise combinations of variables, including working speed, pressure, material type and abrasive load. SCM has encoded this body of qualitative and quantitative data into proprietary algorithms, which the company says deliver more specialised results than generic language models.

The configurator is integrated directly into the workstation’s human-machine interface (HMI), providing responses based on SCM’s operational experience and tailored to individual customer applications.

The system is designed to evolve as new applications are tested under real-world conditions. Each test will add to its knowledge base, allowing SCM to expand and refine the range of solutions available to customers.
Bruno Di Napoli, business unit manager of SCM’s surface treatment solutions, and Sara Iaconianni, SCM’s scouting, idea management and idea generation manager, received the SMAU Innovation Award

“Adopting this configurator brings operational and economic benefits across the entire value chain,” said Alessandro Caramia, product manager and business developer at SCM. “The configurator is designed to reduce setup times and make it easier to set processing parameters, with estimated time savings of up to 20% in the applications considered.”

“Within the company, the tool also guides the sales team in configuring systems optimally during the quotation stage, providing accurate estimates of processing times, costs and productivity, while offering SCM opportunities to develop future software update services,” Caramia said.
